To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the dissipation by inertial modes in spherical shells is dominated by shear layers emitted at the critical latitudes on the inner sphere; these layers excite attractors that are responsible for the large dissipation in the limit of small viscosity.

the viscous dissipated power is a very sensitive function of the forcing frequency in both the two- and three-dimensional models, and that the three-dimensional model shows an additional feature that is not shared by its two-dimensional counterpart: the existence of a frequency interval where the viscous power is independent of the Ekman number.
the response of a rotating fluid to large-scale forcing, which is on the large scale and which is tidal like, is dominated by inertial modes and by the shear layer emitted at the critical latitudes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the response of a viscous fluid inside a spherical container to an imposed tidal forcing.
the dissipation of tidal flows in a spherical shell.
the response of a rotating fluid shell to an imposed tidal-like forcing.

, in the case of a rotating spherical shell, the viscous dissipated power is dominated by the critical latitude shear layer, which in turn is dominated by the attractor associated with the least damped eigenmode.

the three-dimensional solutions show a rich variety of dynamical properties that cannot be captured by their two-dimensional counterparts, and that the dissipation in the full sphere is not very different from the dissipation in a shell of inner radius larger than the critical value.
the dissipation is weak in the three-dimensional case, but it is strong in the two-dimensional case, when the forcing is on the large scale.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dissipation of inertial modes excited by large scale forcing is dominated by the shear layers that are emitted at the critical latitudes on the boundaries.
the response of a rotating fluid shell to large-scale forcing is dominated by inertial modes, which are not necessarily the most damped ones.
, for the case considered here, the two-dimensional model gives the main features of the full three-dimensional problem.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dissipation of inertial modes can be much higher than expected from the dissipation of the eigenmodes, and it can be very sensitive to the frequency of the external forcing.
the viscous dissipated power of the flow is a very sensitive function of the forcing frequency and that the dissipation is not necessarily proportional to viscosity.

, in a rotating fluid shell, the viscous dissipated energy by a tidal-like forcing is very sensitive to the frequency of the tidal forcing and that this sensitivity is due to the excitation of attractors and their associated shear layers.
